proposition: A man stranded for years finds the one thing that survived with him intact, a Mokobara Transit Backpack that still holds his whole life and somehow everything he needs to get home, so the bag becomes both the memory and the way back.

board.style_line: Cinematic 9:16 vertical live-action film, 35mm anamorphic look, warm natural golden-hour light, shallow depth of field, photoreal skin and fabric, faint film grain, castaway-adventure tone with dry physical comedy.
board.negative_line: No text, no logos, no captions, no subtitles, no watermarks, no lettering on any surface, no second bag, no recognisable actors or film characters, no distorted hands, no extra fingers.

identity_anchors.bag: a Mokobara Transit Backpack in Private Island colourway: deep navy matte body, bright yellow lining visible whenever it is open, a vertical front zip and a front bucket pocket each with two black zip pulls, black padded straps, and a small top grab handle; 30-litre size, clean structured shape, no other bag in frame
identity_anchors.castaway: a lean Indian man in his late thirties, sun-darkened skin, long salt-matted black hair and a full unkempt beard, wearing a torn sun-bleached off-white linen shirt and rolled dark trousers, barefoot, ribs slightly showing, bright alert eyes
identity_anchors.island: a small tropical island: blinding white sand, leaning coconut palms, glassy turquoise shallows, one grey volcanic rock outcrop at the far end, a palm trunk near the treeline carved with hundreds of small tally scratches
identity_anchors.photo: a small creased 4x6 print, colours sun-faded, of a smiling Indian woman in a mustard-yellow dupatta photographed from a slight three-quarter angle with soft focus, held between a thumb and forefinger

hero_frame.description: Top-down on white sand at golden hour: the bag sits open, bright yellow lining blazing against the deep navy matte body, and the castaway's right arm is inside it up to the shoulder, his cheek pressed against the top grab handle as he reaches for the bottom. Around the bag, in a neat ring, sits the island: a stack of green coconuts, a full bunch of bananas, leaf-wrapped fish, a coil of rope, a folded tarp, a knife and a compass. The bag is not bulging. The joke and the product claim are the same picture: a 30-litre backpack swallowing an island without changing shape.

audio.music_bed: Surf ambience under a lone nylon-string guitar; the guitar stops dead for the arms-in-the-bag gag (only a zip and a coconut knock are heard), then returns with a warm brass swell for the departure and resolves to one held chord on the close.

beats.title: Years
beats.feeling: Weariness that has settled into routine; this man stopped counting hope a long time ago.
beats.framing: Vertical wide from low on the sand. The castaway sits on the grey volcanic rock at frame centre-right, staring out at an empty horizon. Left of frame, foreground, the carved palm trunk covered in tally scratches runs the full height of the 9:16 frame. Palms sway slowly; a wave slides in and out at the bottom edge; nothing else moves.
beats.first_frame: The castaway seated on the rock, elbows on knees, hair blown sideways; the tally-scratched palm trunk large in the left foreground; empty turquoise sea and a pale sky filling the top half.
beats.impact: Slow push-in of about ten percent over three seconds. Only surf and one distant gull. A single wave crashing at the two-second mark is the beat's only accent; he does not react to it.

beats.title: The tide gives something back
beats.feeling: A jolt: something man-made in a world that has had nothing man-made for years.
beats.framing: Very low angle at the waterline, camera almost on the wet sand. A receding wave drains out of frame toward the top, uncovering a deep navy matte backpack lying on its side, half-buried, its small top grab handle and one black padded strap sticking up out of the sand. A sliver of bright yellow lining shows where the vertical front zip has slid open an inch. In the far background, out of focus, the castaway stands up from the rock.
beats.first_frame: Foam sliding back across the wet sand at the top of frame; the navy bag's grab handle and strap breaking the sand surface at frame centre; the castaway a small blurred figure standing on the rock in the distance.
beats.impact: Locked-off camera; the only motion is the water leaving and the bag being revealed. Sound drops to the hiss of the receding wave, then the guitar enters on its first note exactly as the yellow lining catches the light. He starts running toward camera in the last second.

beats.title: It is his
beats.feeling: Recognition, then the first laugh he has had in years; the bag is unharmed and that is almost unbelievable.
beats.framing: Medium close, handheld feel, the castaway kneeling in the shallows with the bag lifted in both hands at chest height, wet sand pouring off the deep navy matte body. The camera is at his eye level; the bag fills the lower third, his face the middle third. He wipes sand off the front bucket pocket with his forearm and the two black zip pulls swing free. Both black padded straps hang intact.
beats.first_frame: The bag being lifted clear of the water, sand and water streaming off the matte navy surface, the castaway's bearded face just above it, eyes wide, mouth open.
beats.impact: He turns the bag once to check it, then presses it to his chest and laughs silently up at the sky. A short hard zoom in on the laugh. Sound: the slap of wet sand, his breath, the guitar picking up tempo.

beats.title: Her
beats.feeling: Everything he stopped letting himself think about arrives in a single small object.
beats.framing: Close on hands and bag, sitting in the shade at the treeline. He pulls the vertical front zip down its full length and the bright yellow lining glows in the dim shade like a lit window. He reaches into the front bucket pocket and draws out the photo. Camera tilts up with his hands as he lifts the photo to his face; the photo is soft and small in frame, the woman's face turned three-quarters away, never sharp enough to be anyone.
beats.first_frame: The castaway's cracked, sandy fingers on the black zip pull of the vertical front zip, the navy bag on his lap, yellow lining just beginning to show at the top of the zip.
beats.impact: Long unbroken hold on his face as he looks at the photo, then he lowers it and presses it flat against his chest with both hands. Guitar thins to single notes; wind in the palms. He looks from the photo to the sea, and the face changes from grief to decision.

beats.title: Inventory
beats.feeling: Rising delight: the bag keeps giving, and the man is getting his competence back with every item.
beats.framing: Top-down on white sand. The open bag sits at frame centre with its yellow lining facing the sky. The castaway is at the bottom of frame, both arms inside the bag up to the elbows, then the shoulders. Items land one by one in a neat grid around the bag as he pulls them out: a coil of rope, a folding knife, a brass compass, a signal mirror, a folded orange tarp, a steel water bottle, a fire steel, a small first-aid tin. By the end the grid is almost complete and his arms are still inside the bag.
beats.first_frame: Top-down: the bag open at centre, yellow lining bright, the castaway's two hands just entering it, and empty white sand around it.
beats.impact: The grid fills in quick jump-cut rhythm, one item per half-second, each placed with a small satisfying sound (rope thump, knife click, bottle clank). On the last item his arms go in past the shoulders and his beard flattens against the grab handle; the guitar drops out entirely for that half-second.

beats.title: Packing the island
beats.feeling: The gag: the bag should be full and it simply is not; he tests it, the bag wins, he shrugs.
beats.framing: Same top-down setup as beat 5, now surrounded by food: a stack of green coconuts, a full bunch of bananas, three leaf-wrapped fish, a pile of wild mangoes, plus the rope, tarp, knife and compass from before. He feeds the coconuts in first, then the bananas whole, then the fish, pushing each down with a flat hand. The deep navy matte body keeps its clean shape the whole time. The last thing in is his own arm, to the shoulder, checking for room.
beats.first_frame: Top-down: the bag open at centre, bright yellow lining, ringed by the coconuts, banana bunch, fish and gear; the castaway's hand holding the first coconut just above the opening.
beats.impact: Locked camera, real-time speed, no cuts, so the viewer watches the volume go in. Sound is only zips and knocks with the guitar silent. He pauses, looks at the bag, looks at the empty sand around it, and gives the camera a tiny shrug. The '30L' super is composed onto the sand beside the bag for the final second and a half as the punchline.

beats.title: Going home
beats.feeling: Resolve and release; he is leaving the way he came, but carrying everything this time.
beats.framing: Vertical wide from behind, dawn. The castaway wades into the turquoise shallows toward a small driftwood raft with the orange tarp rigged as a sail. The deep navy matte backpack is on his back, black padded straps over the torn linen shirt, the top grab handle catching the sunrise, both black zip pulls on the front bucket pocket swinging. The island's tally-scratched palm is at the left edge of frame; the open sea and a rising orange sun fill the top half.
beats.first_frame: The castaway from behind, ankle-deep in the shallows, the navy bag square on his back against the sea, raft and tarp sail waiting ten metres ahead.
beats.impact: Slow steadicam follow for two seconds, then the camera stops and he keeps going, getting smaller. Brass joins the guitar in a warm swell. He does not look back at the island.

beats.title: Doorstep
beats.feeling: Home, and a last laugh: the man is a wreck, the bag is not.
beats.framing: Medium shot in a Mumbai apartment corridor in evening light, a plain teak door with a brass number plate that carries no legible text. The castaway, still bearded and ragged, sets the deep navy matte backpack down against the door frame and brushes sand off the front bucket pocket with the back of his hand; a single green coconut rolls out of the top and settles on the doormat. The bag stands upright on its own, clean-lined. He reaches for the doorbell and the camera settles on the bag as the door begins to open and warm light spills across it.
beats.first_frame: The castaway in profile at the door, filthy and salt-stained, lowering the pristine navy backpack to the floor; corridor lights warm and soft; door closed.
beats.impact: One quiet take; the coconut roll is the only comic sound. The door-open light is the last motion in the film and it lands on the bag, not on the reunion; the reunion stays off-screen. Music resolves toward the single held chord.

beats.title: Brand close
beats.feeling: Calm confidence; the product finally presented plainly after being the hero of the story.
beats.framing: Code-composed card. The customer product still (transit_backpack_private_island_1) centred on a deep navy field, the mokobara wordmark above it, and the three exact strings composed below in a clean stack: product name, capacity, URL.
beats.first_frame: Product still of the Transit Backpack in Private Island colourway on a deep navy field, wordmark above, no motion.
beats.impact: Cut, not dissolve. Held for the full three seconds on the single resolving chord, then silence for the final half second.

capacity_punchline.why: The joke of beat 6 is that a thirty-litre bag swallows an island; composing the real capacity onto the sand next to the bag as the last coconut goes in turns the gag into the product fact without a claim line.

close_card.why: All three exact strings are required overlays; the composed close card is the only surface where text sits without competing with generated frames, and the URL is the ask.

mandatory.customer_words: lets make an ad with mokobara ... identity_invariants: deep navy matte body, bright yellow lining, vertical front zip and front bucket pocket with two black zip pulls, black padded straps, small top grab handle
mandatory.realisation: The bag is the plot from beat 2 onward and every beat 2 to 8 restates the identity anchor verbatim; the yellow lining is used as the visual reveal in beats 2, 4, 5 and 6; the product still closes the film.

mandatory.customer_words: i would preferably give it the odysey movie angel ... he was on the island where he was kept for years
mandatory.realisation: A generic castaway epic: years established by the tally-scratched palm in beat 1, a lone island, a raft voyage home in beat 7. No names, gods, monsters or scenes from any specific work.

mandatory.customer_words: the protagonist found his mokobara bag, while he was on the island
mandatory.realisation: Beat 2 the tide uncovers it; beat 3 he lifts it, recognises it and laughs.

mandatory.customer_words: in that bag he founds her wives photo
mandatory.realisation: Beat 4: the photo comes out of the front bucket pocket, is held to his chest, and is the reason he decides to leave. The woman is a generated, non-identifiable face shown soft and three-quarter.

mandatory.customer_words: and a lot of stuff that he could use to go back
mandatory.realisation: Beat 5 lays out rope, knife, compass, mirror, tarp, bottle, fire steel and first-aid tin in a grid around the bag; the tarp becomes the raft sail in beat 7.

mandatory.customer_words: he packs food and stuff and goes back
mandatory.realisation: Beat 6 packs coconuts, bananas, fish and mangoes plus the gear; beat 7 he wades to the raft with the bag on; beat 8 he reaches his front door.

mandatory.customer_words: would be funny that he could keep his arms in the bag and food and so much stuff
mandatory.realisation: Beats 5 and 6 put his arms in past the shoulders with his beard flattened on the grab handle, the bag never bulges, and he shrugs at camera; the music drops out for the gag.

mandatory.customer_words: Avoid getting copyright violoations from odysssey
mandatory.realisation: No character, place, god or creature names; no scenes unique to any book or film; the castaway, tally marks, island, photo and raft are public-domain tropes; the negative line bans recognisable actors and film characters.

mandatory.customer_words: exact_text_strings: Transit Backpack, 30L, mokobara.com (overlay, may_reflow false)
mandatory.realisation: Composed by code, never generated: 30L as the punchline super at 19.5 to 21 s and all three strings on the close card at 27 to 30 s.

mandatory.customer_words: aspect 9:16, motion seconds 30, audio true, multi_shot_story, generated
mandatory.realisation: Nine contiguous beats totalling 30 s, all framed vertical, a still then image-to-video per beat, native audio with music and no voice-over.
Both used only on the code-composed close card in beat 9; no logo is ever generated inside a frame.

brand_timeline.in_context: The product is first seen at 3 s as the thing the tide gives back, is on screen in every beat from 2 to 8 as the story's engine, and the wordmark appears only on the composed close at 27 s.
brand_timeline.spoken: none; no voice-over, brand carried visually and by the close card
